To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 3′ UTR of TCV forms a highly interactive structure that supports translation and replication and includes a tRNA-shaped scaffold that is a central element in the regulation of these processes.

the 3′ UTR of TCV is organized into an RNA network that supports translation and replication and that includes a tRNA-shaped scaffold and a ribosomal binding site that is connected to the 5′ end of the genome through an intervening, largely disordered region.

the majority of the 300 nt 3′ untranslated (UTR) region of Turnip crickle virus (TCV, genus Carmovirus, family Tombusviridae) is involved in the regulation of viral translation and replication, and forms a highly interactive network of RNA elements that include the ribosome binding tRNA-shaped structure and the 3′-terminal hairpin.
